exercise.name: Elbow to Knee Side Plank Crunch

reference.title: Elbow to Knee Side Plank Crunch (male)
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the network proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice

exercise.mechanics: Compound (isometric side support with trunk flexion and hip flexion)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the elbow and knee meet, inhale as you return to the straight plank.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s in, short squeeze, 1.2 s out

prescription.tempo: About 1 s in, brief squeeze, 1 s out
prescription.progression: More reps, then a straight-arm side plank

cues.text: Side plank on the right forearm, elbow under the shoulder, feet stacked, hips up in one line. Left fingertips behind the head.
Breathe out and draw the top knee forward and up while the trunk curls down to meet it, elbow to knee.
Short squeeze; keep the hips lifted.
Breathe in and return to the straight side plank, top foot back on the bottom foot.
Repeat; finish the set, then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Hips sagging toward the mat during the crunch
mistakes.fix: Push the floor away with the forearm and keep the bottom hip up.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the head down with the hand
mistakes.fix: Fingertips only; curl from the ribs.
Elbow under the shoulder; press up through the forearm.
About 1 s in, short squeeze, 1 s out.

kinematics.norm: Hips stay lifted in line with the shoulders and feet (clinical opinion)
Trunk curls and turns down toward the knee (clinical opinion)
Knee drawn forward to meet the elbow (clinical opinion)
Elbow directly under the shoulder, forearm on the floor (clinical opinion)
Controlled, a short squeeze each rep (clinical opinion)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Shoulder pain on the supporting side (instability, rotator cuff): start with the knee side plank or skip.
modify: Bottom knee down (knee side plank) while the top knee drives in.
regressions: Knee side plank with the top knee drive.
progressions: Slower reps with a 2 s squeeze.
Side plank on the hand (straight arm) with the knee drive.

muscleNotes.obliques_r: Bottom-side obliques hold the trunk up against gravity as in the side plank (external oblique about 62% MVIC in the side bridge, Escamilla 2016).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Top-side obliques curl and turn the trunk down toward the knee (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis curls the trunk toward the knee (clinical opinion; about 21-26% MVIC just to hold the side bridge, Escamilla 2016).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Draw the top knee forward and up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Bottom-side hip abductors hold the pelvis up (side bridge above 45% MVIC, Ekstrom 2007).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the supporting shoulder blade on the rib cage.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Steadies the supporting shoulder over the elbow.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Steadies the supporting shoulder over the elbow.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff steadies the supporting shoulder.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Helps hold the trunk up on the supporting side (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Stands in for quadratus lumborum, highly active in side support (McGill 1998).

guides.label: Top knee drives to the elbow
